title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄序
士以言揚也乆矣夫言不苟
飾也裕之以學言不苟達也
文之□□言不苟信也副之
□□以□苟□也統之以行
□□是□□□□也篤者之
□□□□□□□言閎以深
===
□□和□□□□□通者之言
□□言□□□□言誕狡者之
□□□□者之言淫中無主
者之□足以達于治猶影響
然是故朝廷之制命宗廟之
聲謌聘問之辭令官府之播
告戎旅之檄諭微而通幽玄
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄序

士以言揚也，乆矣。夫言不苟飾也，裕之以學；言不苟達也，文之□□；言不苟信也，副之□□；以□苟□也，統之以行。□□是□□□□也，篤者之□□□□□□□，言閎以深，□□和□□□□□，通者之言□□，言□□□□言誕，狡者之□□□□，者之言淫，中無主者之□，足以達于治，猶影響然。是故朝廷之制命、宗廟之聲謌、聘問之辭令、官府之播告、戎旅之檄諭，微而通幽玄
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination

It has long been the case that scholars gain recognition through their words. Words must not be carelessly embellished: enrich them through learning. Words must not be carelessly expressed: adorn them with [illegible]. Words must not lightly claim credibility: substantiate them with [illegible]. [Damaged passage, sense uncertain; ?] bring them together through conduct. [Illegible] the words of the earnest [illegible]; words are expansive and profound; [illegible] harmonious [illegible]; the words of those of comprehensive understanding [illegible]; words [illegible] are extravagant; those of the cunning [illegible]; the words of [illegible] are immoderate; those who lack an inner guiding principle [illegible]. [The connection is uncertain; ?] sufficient to contribute to good government, just as shadows and echoes respond. Thus, the court’s decrees and commands, the songs of the ancestral temples, the diplomatic language of formal missions and inquiries, the proclamations of government offices, and the military’s dispatches and admonitions—in their subtle workings, they reach into hidden mysteries…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
顯而昭化理言之義用大矣
洪惟我
朝
聖祖
神宗稽古□治養士有學取士有
科□□□□□博之於子史
徵之於□□□之於積歲而
===
取之於決□□□是錄而後
之□□成□□無遺者嗚呼
盛哉
列聖馭世理人之道至要而至大
存焉爾嘉靖乙酉厥期旣屆
巡按雲南監察御史熊榮議
舉試事而貴州之士亦並敘
punctuated:
顯而昭化理，言之義用大矣！洪惟我朝聖祖神宗，稽古□治，養士有學，取士有科。□□□□□博之於子史，徵之於□□□之於積歲，而取之於決□□□是錄，而後之□□成□□無遺者。嗚呼，盛哉！列聖馭世理人之道，至要而至大，存焉爾。
嘉靖乙酉，厥期旣屆，巡按雲南監察御史熊榮議舉試事，而貴州之士亦並敘
translation_en:
…in its manifest aspects, it illuminates the principles of transformation and order. Great indeed are the significance and uses of words! We reverently consider how our dynasty’s sagely progenitors and divine ancestors consulted antiquity to […] govern [?], maintained schools to nurture scholars, and established examinations to select them. […] They broadened their learning through the philosophical masters and histories, verified it against […] over accumulated years [?], and selected them through a decisive […] this record […] those who came afterward […] accomplished […] none omitted [?]. Ah, how flourishing! Herein lies the successive sage sovereigns’ way of governing the world and ordering the people, supremely essential and supremely great.
In the yiyou year of Jiajing [1525], when the appointed time had arrived, Xiong Rong, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Yunnan, proposed holding the examination; the scholars of Guizhou were also included together…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
焉
制也先是雲南藩臬以具白于巡
撫雲南都御史黃衷旣具則
又白于鎮守雲南太監杜唐
總兵官黔國公沐紹勛咸曰
典也維時巡撫雲南都御史吳祺
繼至益崇優將巡撫貴州都
===
御史楊一漢鎮守太監楊廣
都督僉事牛桓巡按監察御
史鍾卿密尤精志恊德用相
厥成清戎監察御史江良材
事事兩藩振飭益力而前巡
按御史郭楠拓院之規左布
政使楊惟康右布政使鄧相
punctuated: 焉，制也。先是，雲南藩臬以具白于巡撫雲南都御史黃衷，旣具，則又白于鎮守雲南太監杜唐、總兵官黔國公沐紹勛，咸曰：「典也。」維時，巡撫雲南都御史吳祺繼至，益崇優將。巡撫貴州都御史楊一漢、鎮守太監楊廣、都督僉事牛桓、巡按監察御史鍾卿密，尤精志恊德，用相厥成。清戎監察御史江良材，事事兩藩，振飭益力。而前巡按御史郭楠拓院之規，左布政使楊惟康、右布政使鄧相
translation_en:
…therein, as prescribed by the established regulations. Previously, Yunnan’s Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions had reported the arrangements to Huang Zhong, Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yunnan. Once the arrangements were complete, they also reported them to Du Tang, the Grand Eunuch stationed in Yunnan, and Mu Shaoxun, Duke of Qian and Regional Commander. Both declared: “This accords with established precedent.” At this time, Wu Qi arrived to succeed as Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Yunnan, and provided still more generous support [?].

Yang Yihan, Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Guizhou; Yang Guang, the Grand Eunuch stationed there; Niu Huan, Assistant Military Commissioner-in-Chief; and Zhong Qingmi [?], Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, devoted themselves with particular diligence and worked in concord to bring the undertaking to completion. Jiang Liangcai, the Investigating Censor charged with inspecting military administration, attended to affairs in both provinces and exerted still greater effort to put matters in order. As for former Regional Inspector Guo Nan’s plans to enlarge the examination compound, and Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Weikang and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Deng Xiang…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
經始之務亦至是畢矣玆舉
之盛此其大都也仲秋初吉
考試官則儀與訓導王洪同
考試則敎授耿光敎諭吳悌
高鳳山訓導高山各以聘至
提學副使孫繼芳僉事趙淵
預取之士亦旣濡穎而待矣
===
御史榮乃申令于内曰量材
稱事巨細必式參政劉鶴年
參議陳卿司之禁慝戢譁維
典維法按察使葛浩副使盛
儀司之又申令于外曰内供
必節外防必恪參政黃昭道
劉瓚副使陳璋姜龍李潤劉
punctuated:
經始之務，亦至是畢矣。玆舉之盛，此其大都也。仲秋初吉，考試官則儀與訓導王洪，同考試則敎授耿光、敎諭吳悌、高鳳山、訓導高山，各以聘至。提學副使孫繼芳、僉事趙淵預取之士，亦旣濡穎而待矣。
御史榮乃申令于内曰：「量材稱事，巨細必式。」參政劉鶴年、參議陳卿司之。「禁慝戢譁，維典維法。」按察使葛浩、副使盛儀司之。又申令于外曰：「内供必節，外防必恪。」參政黃昭道、劉瓚、副使陳璋、姜龍、李潤、劉
translation_en:
…the work of planning and construction was also completed by this time. Such, in broad outline, was the flourishing state of this examination. At the beginning of the second month of autumn, the Examiners—Yi and Assistant Instructor Wang Hong—and the Associate Examiners—Prefectural School Instructor Geng Guang, County School Instructors Wu Ti and Gao Fengshan, and Assistant Instructor Gao Shan—each arrived in response to an invitation. The candidates previously selected by Sun Jifang, Vice Surveillance Commissioner for Education, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhao Yuan had likewise moistened their brush tips and stood ready.
Censor Rong then reiterated instructions for those inside: “Assess abilities and assign duties accordingly; in matters great and small, follow the prescribed rules.” Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Henian and Administration Assistant Commissioner Chen Qing were in charge of this. “Prevent wrongdoing and quell disturbances, adhering to the statutes and laws.” Surveillance Commissioner Ge Hao and Vice Surveillance Commissioner Sheng Yi were in charge of this. He also reiterated instructions for those outside: “Supplies for the interior must be economical, and security outside must be maintained diligently.” Administration Vice Commissioners Huang Zhaodao and Liu Zan, and Vice Surveillance Commissioners Chen Zhang, Jiang Long, Li Run, and Liu…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
用中沈良佐戴書僉事邵清
傅尚文郭敘楊材司之防維
推拔各殫厥心貴州叅政鄭
錫文于湛叅議江玠李楫按
察使于鏊副使潘鑑僉事楊
薰成周司之宵鉦晝柝偵卒
有翼都指揮方仲胡章張松
===
司之至如揭綱舉維井井絡
絡御史榮之所綜也是月丙
申鎖院丙辰而撤凡三試之
拔士之尤者五十有五人併
其文具錄以
獻儀次當敘儀曩聞諸談者言
秦黔之地率皆異其產而略
punctuated:
用中、沈良佐、戴書、僉事邵清、傅尚文、郭敘、楊材司之。防維推拔，各殫厥心，貴州叅政鄭錫文、于湛、叅議江玠、李楫、按察使于鏊、副使潘鑑、僉事楊薰、成周司之。宵鉦晝柝，偵卒有翼，都指揮方仲、胡章、張松司之。至如揭綱舉維，井井絡絡，御史榮之所綜也。
是月丙申鎖院，丙辰而撤。凡三試之，拔士之尤者五十有五人，併其文具錄以獻。
儀次當敘。儀曩聞諸談者言，秦黔之地，率皆異其產而略
translation_en:
…Yongzhong, Shen Liangzuo, and Dai Shu, together with Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Shao Qing, Fu Shangwen, Guo Xu, and Yang Cai, were responsible for these matters. Maintaining safeguards and selecting outstanding candidates, each devoted his utmost efforts: responsibility lay with Guizhou Administration Vice Commissioners Zheng Xiwen and Yu Zhan, Administration Assistant Commissioners Jiang Jie and Li Ji, Surveillance Commissioner Yu Ao, Vice Surveillance Commissioner Pan Jian, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Yang Xun and Cheng Zhou. Gongs sounded at night and watch-clappers by day; watchful soldiers stood ready to assist. Regional Military Commissioners Fang Zhong, Hu Zhang, and Zhang Song were responsible for this. As for holding together the guiding threads and ensuring that everything was orderly and interconnected, this was under the overall direction of Censor Rong.
On the bingshen day of that month, the examination compound was sealed; on the bingchen day, the restrictions were lifted. Three sessions were held in all, and fifty-five of the most outstanding candidates were selected. Their writings were also recorded in full for presentation to the throne.
It fell in turn to me, Yi, to write the preface. I had formerly heard people discussing the lands of Qin and Qian [?]: they generally regarded their products as remarkable, while overlooking…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
乎其才竊甞疑焉而未有言
也頃道辰沅歴鎭遠帶甲控
弦之衞連絡不絕椎結革裘
之子蹻捷上下虎關鳥道盤
廻數千里每陟益峻勢益嶮
而觀益竒躋雲躡霧者踰月
而達則豁然大觀閉者以融
===
隱者以燦炎濁之氣灑然高
寒視江南都會形便特勝因
仰而嘆曰嘻壯哉使談者之
言而信數千里之所盤廻峻
者嶮者觀而竒者閉而融者
隱而燦者則其所産豈但燐
然而光沃然而澤雜然而變
punctuated: 乎其才，竊甞疑焉，而未有言也。頃道辰沅，歴鎭遠，帶甲控弦之衞連絡不絕，椎結革裘之子蹻捷上下。虎關鳥道，盤廻數千里，每陟益峻，勢益嶮，而觀益竒。躋雲躡霧者踰月而達，則豁然大觀，閉者以融，隱者以燦。炎濁之氣，灑然高寒，視江南都會，形便特勝。因仰而嘆曰：「嘻，壯哉！使談者之言而信，數千里之所盤廻，峻者、嶮者、觀而竒者、閉而融者、隱而燦者，則其所産豈但燐然而光、沃然而澤、雜然而變
translation_en:
…their talent. I had privately long doubted this, but had said nothing. Recently I travelled through Chen and Yuan and passed through Zhenyuan. Garrisons of men clad in armor and drawing bows followed one another without a break, while men with mallet-shaped topknots and leather coats climbed and descended with nimble steps. Through tiger passes and bird paths, I wound my way for several thousand li. With each ascent the slopes grew steeper, the terrain more perilous, and the sights more wondrous. After more than a month of climbing through clouds and treading through mist, I arrived, and suddenly a vast prospect opened before me: what had been enclosed opened out, and what had been hidden shone forth. The hot, murky air gave way to the refreshing chill of high elevations. Compared with the great cities of Jiangnan, this place was especially superior in its terrain and advantages of location.
Then I looked up and exclaimed: “Ah, how magnificent! If what those speakers say were indeed true, then, throughout these several thousand li of winding travel—with their steepness, their perils, their wondrous sights, their enclosures opening out, and their hidden things shining forth—could what this land produces be merely things that gleam with radiance, abound in richness, and mingle in variety…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
獻之學誠裕矣才誠文矣物誠
副矣
聖朝文教旁被無外此亦足證而
信矣然統之以行則有司有
深懼焉尚勉乎哉脩於家而
不壞於
天子之庭者是則士行之良者也
===
其尚勉乎哉無以燐然之光
沃然之澤雜然之變之物卒
於玩而已矣
四川成都府新都縣儒學教
諭劉儀謹序
punctuated:
獻之學誠裕矣，才誠文矣，物誠副矣。聖朝文教旁被無外，此亦足證而信矣。然統之以行，則有司有深懼焉。尚勉乎哉！脩於家而不壞於天子之庭者，是則士行之良者也。其尚勉乎哉！無以燐然之光、沃然之澤、雜然之變之物，卒於玩而已矣。
四川成都府新都縣儒學教諭劉儀謹序。
translation_en:
…the learning presented is truly ample, the talent truly cultivated, and the substance truly commensurate [?]. The civilizing influence of our sagely dynasty extends everywhere, leaving no place beyond its reach; this, too, provides sufficient evidence to make that credible. Yet when these qualities are brought together under the standard of conduct, the responsible officials have profound apprehensions. Strive still further! Those who cultivate themselves at home and remain uncorrupted at the Son of Heaven’s court exemplify good conduct among scholars. Strive still further! Do not let things of glittering brilliance, rich luster, and manifold variation end up as mere objects of amusement.
Preface respectfully composed by Liu Yi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan.

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史熊榮〔以仁河南光山縣人丁丑進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉鶴年〔惟新四川巴縣人戊辰進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參議陳卿〔汝忠四川宜賓縣人乙丑進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使包溥〔天宏浙江上虞縣人丙辰進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司副使盛儀〔德章直隸江都縣人乙丑進士〕
===
考試官
四川成都府新都縣儒學教諭劉儀〔來鳳湖廣安陸州奉祠所人癸酉貢士〕
江西南昌府儒學訓導王洪〔大器湖廣江夏縣人癸酉貢士〕
同考試官
浙江衢州府儒學教授耿光〔謙甫湖廣麻城縣人辛酉貢士〕
江西袁州府宜春縣儒學教諭吳悌〔大友福建南靖縣人己卯貢士〕
湖廣長沙府攸縣儒學教諭高鳳山〔瑞鎮福建安溪縣人己卯貢士〕
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學訓導高山〔仰止福建甌寧縣人己卯貢士〕
印卷官
punctuated:
嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試

監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史熊榮〔以仁，河南光山縣人，丁丑進士〕。

提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參政劉鶴年〔惟新，四川巴縣人，戊辰進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司右參議陳卿〔汝忠，四川宜賓縣人，乙丑進士〕。

監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使包溥〔天宏，浙江上虞縣人，丙辰進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司副使盛儀〔德章，直隸江都縣人，乙丑進士〕。

考試官
四川成都府新都縣儒學教諭劉儀〔來鳳，湖廣安陸州奉祠所人，癸酉貢士〕。
江西南昌府儒學訓導王洪〔大器，湖廣江夏縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

同考試官
浙江衢州府儒學教授耿光〔謙甫，湖廣麻城縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
江西袁州府宜春縣儒學教諭吳悌〔大友，福建南靖縣人，己卯貢士〕。
湖廣長沙府攸縣儒學教諭高鳳山〔瑞鎮，福建安溪縣人，己卯貢士〕。
直隸鎮江府丹徒縣儒學訓導高山〔仰止，福建甌寧縣人，己卯貢士〕。

印卷官
translation_en:

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
鄉人皆好之何如子曰未可也鄉人皆惡
之何如子曰未可也不如鄉人之善
者好之其不善者惡之
莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子慎其獨也
君正莫不正一正君而國定矣
易
包荒得尚于中行以光大也
===
利用爲大作元吉无咎
與天地相似故不違知周乎萬物而道濟
天下故不過旁行而不流樂天知命
故不憂安土敦乎仁故能愛
爻也者效此者也象也者像此者也
書
敷納以言明庶以功
終始慎厥與惟明明后先王惟時懋敬厥
德克配上帝今王嗣有令緒尚監茲
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「鄉人皆好之，何如？」子曰：「未可也。」「鄉人皆惡之，何如？」子曰：「未可也。不如鄉人之善者好之，其不善者惡之。」

莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。

君正，莫不正；一正君，而國定矣。

易

包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。

利用爲大作，元吉，无咎。

與天地相似，故不違；知周乎萬物，而道濟天下，故不過；旁行而不流，樂天知命，故不憂；安土敦乎仁，故能愛。

爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。

書

敷納以言，明庶以功。

終始慎厥與，惟明明后。先王惟時懋敬厥德，克配上帝。今王嗣有令緒，尚監茲
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“If everyone in his village likes him, what of it?” The Master said, “That is not sufficient.” “If everyone in his village dislikes him, what of it?” The Master said, “That is not sufficient. Better that the good people of his village should like him and the bad people dislike him.”

Nothing is more visible than what is hidden, and nothing more manifest than what is minute. Therefore, the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.

“When the ruler is upright, none will fail to be upright. Once the ruler is set right, the state will be settled.”

Book of Changes

“Embracing what is uncultivated, one gains esteem through the middle course”: this is because of one's radiance and greatness.

“It is favorable to undertake great works. Supreme good fortune; no blame.”

He accords with Heaven and Earth and therefore does not run counter to them. His understanding encompasses the myriad things, and his Way brings aid to all under Heaven; therefore, he does not err. He ranges widely without going astray. He delights in Heaven and understands his allotted destiny; therefore, he has no anxiety. He is content where he dwells and steadfast in benevolence; therefore, he can love.

The lines are what reproduce these things; the images are what represent these things.

Book of Documents

“Receive them widely on the basis of their words, and distinguish them all by their accomplishments.”

“From beginning to end, be careful about those with whom you associate: only an enlightened ruler discerns this clearly. The former king diligently revered his virtue and was able to match the Lord on High. Now you, O king, have inherited his splendid legacy. May you take this as your mirror…”

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
哉若升高必自下若陟遐必自邇無
輕民事惟難無安厥位惟危慎終于
始有言逆于汝心必求諸道有言遜
于汝志必求諸非道嗚呼弗慮胡獲
弗為胡成一人元良萬邦以貞
次五曰建用皇極次六曰乂用三德
明王立政不惟其官惟其人
詩
寬兮綽兮猗重較兮
===
鴥彼飛隼其飛戾天亦集爰止方叔涖止
其車三千師干之試方叔率止鉦人
伐鼓陳師鞠旅顯允方叔伐鼓淵淵
振旅闐闐
夙興夜寐洒埽廷内維民之章
維清緝熙文王之典肇禋迄用有成維周
之禎
春秋
齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕盟于召
punctuated:
哉！若升高，必自下；若陟遐，必自邇。無輕民事，惟難；無安厥位，惟危。慎終于始。有言逆于汝心，必求諸道；有言遜于汝志，必求諸非道。嗚呼！弗慮胡獲？弗為胡成？一人元良，萬邦以貞。
次五曰建用皇極，次六曰乂用三德。
明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。
詩
寬兮綽兮，猗重較兮。
鴥彼飛隼，其飛戾天，亦集爰止。方叔涖止，其車三千。師干之試，方叔率止。鉦人伐鼓，陳師鞠旅。顯允方叔，伐鼓淵淵，振旅闐闐。
夙興夜寐，洒埽廷内，維民之章。
維清緝熙，文王之典。肇禋，迄用有成，維周之禎。
春秋
齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕。盟于召
translation_en:
…heed this! To climb high, you must begin below; to journey far, you must begin nearby. Do not take the people's affairs lightly: consider their difficulty. Do not rest secure in your position: consider its peril. From the outset, take care for the end. When words run counter to your heart, you must seek whether they accord with the Way; when words accord with your wishes, you must seek whether they depart from the Way. Alas! Without reflection, how can anything be gained? Without action, how can anything be accomplished? When the one ruler is supremely good, the myriad states are thereby set right.
The fifth is to establish and employ the August Standard; the sixth is to govern through the Three Virtues.
When an enlightened king establishes his government, his concern is not merely with offices, but with the men who fill them.
Book of Odes
How generous, how ample in bearing! He leans upon his carriage's double crossbars.
Swift flies that falcon; its flight reaches heaven, yet it also alights and rests here. Fang Shu has arrived, with three thousand chariots. His troops are practiced in warfare; Fang Shu leads them. The gong officers beat the drums; they array the troops and muster the hosts. Illustrious and trustworthy is Fang Shu! The drums sound deep and resonant; the troops return in formation amid a thunderous din.
Rise early and retire late; sprinkle and sweep within the courtyard. Be a model for the people.
How pure and ever bright are King Wen's statutes! From the first sacrificial offerings, they have brought achievement down to the present: this is Zhou's auspicious blessing.
Spring and Autumn Annals
The Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei reached a mutual agreement at Pu. 〔Third year of Duke Huan.〕 A covenant was concluded at Zhao…

Thus Heaven does not withhold its Way, Earth does not withhold its treasures, and people do not withhold their true feelings.
Singing is giving direct expression to oneself [?] and setting forth virtue.
The people regard the ruler as their heart; the ruler regards the people as his body.

text:
詔誥表內科一道

判語五條

問人君爲文與韋布不同貴乎達之於政
也然政亦多端而孔子謂治天下國家
有九經果足以盡之乎夫唐虞三代之

One topic from among edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials [?].

Third Session.

Question: A ruler’s literary composition differs from that of commoners: what matters is putting it into practice in government. Yet government has many aspects. Confucius spoke of nine guiding principles for governing the world, states, and families: are these truly sufficient to encompass them all? The writings of the rulers of Tang and Yu and of the Three Dynasties are fully recorded in the “Canons” and “Counsels” of the Book of Documents; they cannot be equaled. Although at that time there had not yet …

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
有九經之說而不知行政之實亦果九
經之所能該乎文之與政可岐而爲二
乎嗣後若漢唐宋號稱英主之文亦嘗
纂集矣有曰號令文章煥然可述者有
曰爲文賦詩贍麗冲邁者有曰援翰屬
思極其精妙者不知果有合於九經否
乎我
太祖高皇帝濬本生知動符經典化筆妙於神
授心學得於自然
===
嘉言聖謨衣被海宇而槩見於
御製文集其所以心同孔子治合九經非徒託
之空言而悉見於實政者可得而條陳
乎諸生涵濡
聖化蓋亦有年願鋪張之以爲
聖明法
祖圖治之一助
問我
孝宗敬皇帝大明會典一書蓋倣周禮而作者
punctuated:
有九經之說，而不知行政之實亦果九經之所能該乎？文之與政，可岐而爲二乎？嗣後若漢唐宋號稱英主之文，亦嘗纂集矣。有曰「號令文章煥然可述」者，有曰「爲文賦詩贍麗冲邁」者，有曰「援翰屬思極其精妙」者，不知果有合於九經否乎？我太祖高皇帝濬本生知，動符經典，化筆妙於神授，心學得於自然。嘉言聖謨衣被海宇，而槩見於御製文集。其所以心同孔子、治合九經，非徒託之空言而悉見於實政者，可得而條陳乎？諸生涵濡聖化，蓋亦有年，願鋪張之，以爲聖明法祖圖治之一助。
問：我孝宗敬皇帝《大明會典》一書，蓋倣周禮而作者，
translation_en:
…there was a formulation of the Nine Guidelines; yet were the actual practices of government indeed all encompassed by these Nine Guidelines? Can literary composition and government be divided into two separate things? Subsequently, the writings of those acclaimed as illustrious rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song were also compiled. Of one it was said, “His edicts and writings shone brilliantly and deserved to be transmitted”; of another, “His prose and poetry were rich and beautiful, serene and lofty”; and of another, “When he took up his brush and marshalled his thoughts, he attained the utmost refinement.” But did these writings actually accord with the Nine Guidelines?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao, drawing upon a profound foundation of innate knowledge, accorded with the classics in his every action. His transforming brush possessed a subtlety bestowed by Heaven, and his learning of the mind came naturally. His excellent words and sagely counsels spread their beneficence throughout the realm and are broadly represented in the Collected Imperial Writings. Can you set out, point by point, how his mind was one with that of Confucius and his government accorded with the Nine Guidelines, finding expression entirely in actual governance rather than merely being entrusted to empty words? You candidates have been steeped in the sage influence for many years. We ask you to expound upon this fully, thereby helping our enlightened sovereign to model himself on his ancestor and seek good government.
Question: The book Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) of our Emperor Xiaozong Jing was composed on the model of the Rites of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
幾憂勤惕厲於治心涖政之間而不敢
少忽蓋治亂之所由分理欲之所由定
勢不容不然者三代之君能及時審幾
者具在簡策可悉陳也繼是以後史稱
功德兼隆由漢以來未之有者則歸之
唐太宗貞觀政要所紀信乎比迹湯武
庶幾成康但考貞觀十年之後志業舉
措多不若登極之初其近臣進規則曰
頃歲以來漸不克終又曰千載休期時
===
難再得若甚有所不滿者豈臣子之於
君父故盡責難之忠乎抑太宗隨宜通
變而別有所見乎亦氣數人品自有所
限乎當可為之時失防微之漸良可惜
也諸生讀史至此獨不槩於中乎備言
其故明著于篇
問先正有言賢才出國將昌固也然賢才
而不用亦將昌其國乎三代而下得人
之盛無如漢之武帝賢才之盛無如宋
punctuated:
幾，憂勤惕厲於治心涖政之間，而不敢少忽。蓋治亂之所由分，理欲之所由定，勢不容不然者。三代之君能及時審幾者，具在簡策，可悉陳也。繼是以後，史稱功德兼隆、由漢以來未之有者，則歸之唐太宗。《貞觀政要》所紀，信乎比迹湯武，庶幾成康。但考貞觀十年之後，志業舉措多不若登極之初。其近臣進規，則曰：「頃歲以來，漸不克終。」又曰：「千載休期，時難再得。」若甚有所不滿者。豈臣子之於君父，故盡責難之忠乎？抑太宗隨宜通變，而別有所見乎？亦氣數人品自有所限乎？當可為之時，失防微之漸，良可惜也。諸生讀史至此，獨不槩於中乎？備言其故，明著于篇。
問：先正有言：「賢才出，國將昌。」固也。然賢才而不用，亦將昌其國乎？三代而下，得人之盛，無如漢之武帝；賢才之盛，無如宋
translation_en:
…incipient signs [?], remaining diligent, vigilant, and resolute in governing the mind and administering affairs, without daring the slightest neglect. For this is where order and disorder diverge, and where principle and desire are distinguished; circumstances permit no other course. Accounts of rulers of the Three Dynasties who could discern incipient developments in good time are fully preserved in the written records and can be set forth in detail. Thereafter, the ruler whom the histories credit with achievements and virtue alike so exalted that none since the Han had equaled them is Tang Taizong. Does what is recorded in Essentials of Government of the Zhenguan Reign (Zhenguan zhengyao) truly show that his deeds matched those of Tang and Wu and approached those of Cheng and Kang? Yet, examining the period after the tenth year of Zhenguan, we find that his aspirations, undertakings, and actions often fell short of those at the beginning of his reign. His close ministers offered admonitions, saying, “In recent years, you have gradually become unable to carry through to the end.” They also said, “An auspicious opportunity occurring once in a thousand years is hard to obtain again.” They seem to have been deeply dissatisfied. Was it that, as subjects addressing their ruler and father, they deliberately fulfilled their loyal duty to demand difficult achievements of him? Or did Taizong adapt to circumstances and changing conditions, having some different insight? Or were historical destiny and his personal character inherently limited? It is truly regrettable that, at a time when accomplishment was possible, he failed to guard against trouble at its earliest beginnings. When you students read the histories at this point, are you not moved in your hearts? Explain the reasons fully and set them out clearly in your essays.
Question: A worthy predecessor said, “When worthy and talented men emerge, the state will flourish.” Certainly so. Yet if worthy and talented men are not employed, will they still bring prosperity to their state? Since the Three Dynasties, none equaled Emperor Wu of the Han in the abundance of men he recruited; and none equaled the Song … in the abundance of worthy and talented men.

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之神宗其所以致之者有其由乎其間
道學文章忠義政事具有品目就而論
之孰爲一世之才孰爲百世之才乎合
而較之孰焉尤盛孰焉不及乎說者謂
史臣於武帝獨不言相而宋臣於神宗
亦明言其無將豈天之降才爾殊否乎
夷考其時以道學文章名家者徒多小
試豈不足於政事乎以忠義政事名世
者不獲大用豈或愧於文學乎夫二君
===
者皆負大有爲之志其於文學忠義之
臣亦知首舉尊禮敬納其言愛重其文
矣何君臣之間終於不遇乎豈其君心
之有蔽乎抑有蔽賢者左右於其間乎
若使二君移任柄臣之心以任諸賢其
治效可比隆於三代乎諸生其明以告
我
問雲南古梁州之南境貴州本西南羅施
地也雖距京師萬有餘里而衣冠文物
punctuated:
之神宗。其所以致之者，有其由乎？其間道學、文章、忠義、政事，具有品目。就而論之，孰爲一世之才，孰爲百世之才乎？合而較之，孰焉尤盛，孰焉不及乎？說者謂史臣於武帝獨不言相，而宋臣於神宗亦明言其無將，豈天之降才爾殊否乎？夷考其時，以道學、文章名家者，徒多小試，豈不足於政事乎？以忠義、政事名世者，不獲大用，豈或愧於文學乎？夫二君者，皆負大有爲之志，其於文學、忠義之臣，亦知首舉尊禮，敬納其言，愛重其文矣。何君臣之間終於不遇乎？豈其君心之有蔽乎？抑有蔽賢者左右於其間乎？若使二君移任柄臣之心以任諸賢，其治效可比隆於三代乎？諸生其明以告我。

問：雲南，古梁州之南境；貴州，本西南羅施地也。雖距京師萬有餘里，而衣冠文物
translation_en:
…Shenzong of the Song. Were there particular reasons why he attracted such men? Among them were men distinguished in learning of the Way, literary composition, loyalty and righteousness, and governmental affairs, each with their respective standing. Considering them individually, who possessed talent for one age, and who possessed talent for a hundred ages? Comparing the two groups as a whole, which was more flourishing, and which fell short? Commentators say that the historians, in treating Emperor Wu, conspicuously make no mention of a chief minister, while Song officials explicitly stated that Shenzong had no generals. Could Heaven have bestowed talent so unevenly? On examining those times, we find that men renowned for learning of the Way and literary composition were often given only minor opportunities to prove themselves. Were they unequal to governmental affairs? Men celebrated in their age for loyalty and righteousness and for governmental affairs were not entrusted with major responsibilities. Could they have fallen short in literary learning? Both rulers aspired to great achievements. They knew to give priority to promoting ministers distinguished for literary learning, loyalty, and righteousness, to honor them with due courtesy, to receive their words respectfully, and to cherish their writings. Why, then, did ruler and minister ultimately fail to find fulfillment in one another? Was the ruler’s judgment clouded? Or were there people close at hand who obstructed worthy men? Had these two rulers transferred the trust they placed in their powerful ministers to the worthy men, could the achievements of their government have rivaled the flourishing rule of the Three Dynasties? You candidates should explain this clearly to me.

Question: Yunnan was the southern borderland of ancient Liangzhou; Guizhou was originally the territory of Luoshi in the southwest. Although more than ten thousand li from the capital, its elite culture and cultivated institutions…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
漸與內地相埒惟土夷種落錯雜居民
聲教固已宿遵猖狂時或恣騁古人制
馭之法不過曰羈縻曰撫綏曰脩文德
曰擇信臣而已然性偏氣梗恩被而罔
知法寬而反玩固非一朝夕矣玆欲掃
蕩峒穴慮涉俱焚之殃抑欲疎闊繩銜
或致奔踶之擾夫在虞夏盛時固無戎
狄之患而亦有三苗之冥雖聖人惠風
廣被澤覃幽荒脫不幸而梗吾德化焉
===
蓋必有所處之矣體其情參以法而
酌其時當如何而後可
punctuated: 漸與內地相埒。惟土夷種落錯雜居民，聲教固已宿遵，猖狂時或恣騁。古人制馭之法，不過曰羈縻、曰撫綏、曰脩文德、曰擇信臣而已。然性偏氣梗，恩被而罔知，法寬而反玩，固非一朝夕矣。玆欲掃蕩峒穴，慮涉俱焚之殃；抑欲疎闊繩銜，或致奔踶之擾。夫在虞夏盛時，固無戎狄之患，而亦有三苗之冥。雖聖人惠風廣被，澤覃幽荒，脫不幸而梗吾德化焉，蓋必有所處之矣。體其情，參以法，而酌其時，當如何而後可？
translation_en:
…are gradually coming to rival those of the interior. Yet the indigenous tribal groups live intermingled with the inhabitants. Although they have long acknowledged imperial instruction and moral teaching, they sometimes give free rein to unruly conduct. The ancients’ methods of governing them amounted only to loose rein, pacification, cultivation of civil virtue, and selection of trustworthy ministers. Yet their disposition is wayward and their temper obstinate: they receive benevolence without appreciating it, and respond to lenient laws by flouting them. This has certainly been so for more than a day or an evening. If we now wish to sweep through their cave strongholds, we fear the calamity of indiscriminate destruction; if instead we loosen the reins and bit, we may bring about the disturbance of bolting and kicking.

In the flourishing age of Yu and Xia, there was indeed no trouble from the Rong and Di, yet there was still the benightedness of the Sanmiao. Although the beneficent influence of the sages spread widely and their bounty reached remote wildernesses, should these peoples unfortunately resist our moral transformation, there must surely be some way to deal with them. Taking account of their circumstances, consulting the law, and weighing the needs of the time, what should be done to achieve a fitting resolution?

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
鄉人皆好之何如子曰未可也鄉人皆惡
之何如子曰未可也不如鄉人之善者
好之其不善者惡之
趙鼐
同考試官訓導高批題本平易但字面
複出檃括爲難士子率爲所窘是
篇體認親切而文復合作宜錄出
之
考試官訓導王批詞不費而理自明
□處識見不凡當是佳士
考試官教諭劉批先儒謂學者當將
問處便作已問答處便作已答此
作有之
賢者欲以好惡之同而取人聖人告以不當于
其同而當于其類也盖人之善惡各以其類爲
好惡也觀其類可以知其人矣何必泥于同哉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「鄉人皆好之，何如？」子曰：「未可也。」「鄉人皆惡之，何如？」子曰：「未可也。不如鄉人之善者好之，其不善者惡之。」

趙鼐

同考試官訓導高批：題本平易，但字面複出，檃括爲難，士子率爲所窘。是篇體認親切，而文復合作，宜錄出之。

考試官訓導王批：詞不費而理自明，□處識見不凡，當是佳士。

考試官教諭劉批：先儒謂學者當將問處便作已問，答處便作已答，此作有之。

賢者欲以好惡之同而取人，聖人告以不當于其同，而當于其類也。盖人之善惡，各以其類爲好惡也。觀其類，可以知其人矣，何必泥于同哉？
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Suppose everyone in his village likes him. What would you think of him?” The Master said, “That is not sufficient.” “Suppose everyone in his village dislikes him. What would you think of him?” The Master said, “That is not sufficient. Better that the good people in his village should like him and those who are not good should dislike him.”

Zhao Nai

Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Assistant Instructor: The topic is fundamentally straightforward, but its repeated wording makes it difficult to draw together, and candidates are generally hampered by this. This essay shows an intimate grasp of its meaning, and its composition also meets the requirements. It deserves to be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: Without wasting words, it makes the principle clear of itself. In the □ passages [?], the discernment is exceptional. The author must be a fine scholar.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Earlier Confucian scholars said that learners should treat the questions as questions they themselves had asked, and the answers as answers they themselves had given. This composition achieves that.

The worthy man wished to judge people by unanimity in liking and disliking them. The sage told him that the judgment should rest on the kind of people expressing those feelings, rather than on their unanimity. For people, whether good or bad, each like and dislike others according to their own kind. By observing the kind of people who like or dislike someone, one can know what that person is like. Why insist on unanimity?

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
宜夫子以是答子貢之問也想子貢之意若曰
一鄉之衆論亦公矣有人於此凡鄉之人皆以
為可欲而好之焉是亦能得衆者也其人果何
如乎夫子告之曰行之苟合者毎見悅於衆也
衆好之必察焉而後可豈可據以為賢乎子貢
又曰鄉人皆好固未可矣如或舉鄉之人皆與
其相忤而惡之焉是亦能違俗者也不知其人
何如夫子告之曰人之詭世者毎見憎於衆也
衆惡之必察焉而後可豈可執以為是乎夫鄉
===
人皆好之孰若鄉人之善者好之立志不群者
與其志之同行道有得者嘉其道之合好之者
善人則見好者必非不善人也使無可好之實
善者何為而好之哉鄉人皆惡之孰若鄉人之
不善者惡之以私滅公者疾其不為黨縱欲敗
度者憎其不相比惡之者不善人則見惡者必
其為善人也使有苟合之行不善者何為而惡
之哉是則合衆觀情或至失於徇人分類求情
庶有符於公論汝賜也豈可泥其同而不觀其
punctuated: 宜夫子以是答子貢之問也。想子貢之意若曰：「一鄉之衆論亦公矣。有人於此，凡鄉之人皆以為可欲而好之焉，是亦能得衆者也，其人果何如乎？」夫子告之曰：「行之苟合者毎見悅於衆也。衆好之，必察焉而後可，豈可據以為賢乎？」子貢又曰：「鄉人皆好，固未可矣。如或舉鄉之人皆與其相忤而惡之焉，是亦能違俗者也，不知其人何如？」夫子告之曰：「人之詭世者毎見憎於衆也。衆惡之，必察焉而後可，豈可執以為是乎？夫鄉人皆好之，孰若鄉人之善者好之？立志不群者與其志之同，行道有得者嘉其道之合。好之者善人，則見好者必非不善人也。使無可好之實，善者何為而好之哉？鄉人皆惡之，孰若鄉人之不善者惡之？以私滅公者疾其不為黨，縱欲敗度者憎其不相比。惡之者不善人，則見惡者必其為善人也。使有苟合之行，不善者何為而惡之哉？是則合衆觀情，或至失於徇人；分類求情，庶有符於公論。汝賜也，豈可泥其同而不觀其
translation_en: …It was fitting that the Master should answer Zigong’s question in this way. We may imagine Zigong’s meaning as follows: “The collective judgment of an entire village must surely be impartial. Suppose there is someone whom everyone in the village finds desirable and likes. Such a person can indeed win the people’s approval. What, then, is he really like?” The Master told him: “Those whose conduct seeks indiscriminately to please others often find favor with the multitude. When everyone likes someone, one must investigate before reaching a judgment. How could one take this alone as grounds for considering him worthy?” Zigong asked further: “That everyone in the village likes him is admittedly insufficient. But suppose everyone in the village is at odds with him and dislikes him. Such a person can indeed stand against prevailing customs. I wonder what he is like?” The Master told him: “Those who act perversely against the ways of the world are often hated by the multitude. When everyone dislikes someone, one must investigate before reaching a judgment. How could one insist on taking this as proof that he is in the right? For everyone in the village to like him—how could that compare with the good people of the village liking him? Those whose aspirations set them apart from the crowd approve of him because his aspirations accord with theirs; those who have attained something through practicing the Way commend him because his Way agrees with theirs. If those who like him are good people, then the person they like surely cannot be a bad person. If he had no substance deserving their affection, why would good people like him? For everyone in the village to dislike him—how could that compare with the bad people of the village disliking him? Those who destroy the public good for private ends resent him for refusing to join their faction; those who indulge their desires and undermine proper standards hate him for refusing to side with them. If those who dislike him are bad people, then the person they dislike must be a good person. If his conduct were merely accommodating, why would bad people dislike him? Thus, to consider people’s sentiments by taking the multitude together may lead to the error of yielding to others’ opinions; to seek their true sentiments by distinguishing their kinds may bring one into accord with impartial judgment. You, Ci, how can you cling to their unanimity without examining their …

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
類邪大抵人性有善而無惡故人情好善而惡
惡唯君子爲能約情以合於中小人則欲動情
勝而所好惡遂與人遠矣故觀人者宜於此致
審而脩己者亦宜以是自考也子貢方人而悅
不若己者其於好惡之情非惟審之未真抑恐
發之未能自慊也夫子教之而後聞性與天道
嗚呼聞性矣而情有不中節者乎
莫見乎隱莫顯乎微故君子慎其獨也
余秬
===
同考試官教諭高批道理隱微不爲窘
束是固有獨見者
同考試官教諭吳批說理之文難於明
著此篇易人所難錄出以式多士
考試官訓導王批不爲隱僻語而自
足以發
考試官教諭劉批理因詞見意由文
顯蓋善作者
中庸即人心難掩之幾示君子自省之要蓋人
punctuated:
類邪？大抵人性有善而無惡，故人情好善而惡惡。唯君子爲能約情以合於中，小人則欲動情勝，而所好惡遂與人遠矣。故觀人者宜於此致審，而脩己者亦宜以是自考也。子貢方人而悅不若己者，其於好惡之情，非惟審之未真，抑恐發之未能自慊也。夫子教之，而後聞性與天道。嗚呼！聞性矣，而情有不中節者乎？
莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。
余秬

同考試官教諭吳批：說理之文，難於明著。此篇易人所難，錄出以式多士。
考試官訓導王批：不爲隱僻語，而自足以發。
考試官教諭劉批：理因詞見，意由文顯，蓋善作者。
《中庸》即人心難掩之幾，示君子自省之要。蓋人
translation_en:
…the kinds to which they belong? Generally speaking, human nature contains goodness and no evil; thus human feelings favor goodness and detest evil. Only the gentleman can restrain his feelings so that they accord with the mean. In the petty man, desires stir and feelings prevail, so that his likes and dislikes become far removed from those of others. Thus those who assess people should examine this carefully, while those who cultivate themselves should also use it to examine themselves. Zigong judged others and took pleasure in those inferior to himself. Regarding the feelings of liking and disliking, not only was his discernment not yet sound; one fears that their expression could not yet satisfy his own conscience. Only after the Master instructed him did he hear about human nature and the Way of Heaven. Ah! Once one has heard about human nature, could one’s feelings fail to attain their proper measure?
“Nothing is more manifest than what is hidden; nothing is more evident than what is minute. Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.”
Yu Ju 余秬
Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Instructor: The principles are subtle and hidden, yet the treatment is not cramped. This is certainly someone with insight of his own.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: In writing that expounds principles, clear exposition is difficult. This essay makes easy what others find difficult. It is transcribed here to serve as a model for the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: Without using obscure or recondite language, it is fully adequate to elucidate the meaning.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The principles emerge through the phrasing, and the meaning becomes evident through the composition. He is indeed an accomplished writer.

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
心之幾莫昭於隱微而省察之要莫切於謹獨
也能致慎而不忽焉尚何離道之遠哉中庸論
率性之道以明由教而入至此蓋謂道具于心
固當養於未動之時尤當省於方動之始何則
幽暗之中踪跡邃密人莫能窺其際可謂隱也
然念慮初萌而邪正攸判人雖不覩也已則了
然於胸中見之之真莫可得而掩矣舉天下之
著見者孰有過於隱乎細微之事端緒眇忽人
莫能測其機可謂微也然思惟甫動而善惡遂
===
分人雖未聞也已則昭然於方寸知之之切莫
可得而揜矣極天下之明顯者孰有踰於微乎
夫幾微之動明著如此苟或肆焉則人欲滋長
於獨知之際而馴至離道之遠矣是以君子既
嘗戒懼矣而於此尤加謹焉因其所發之初隨
致省察之力一念之邪即遏絕之務使邪不得
以撓正而惕乎儆戒之弗寧不以人所不知而
侈然以自放也因其方萌之始隨加點檢之功
一念之惡即禁制之務期惡不得以混善而凛
punctuated: 心之幾莫昭於隱微，而省察之要莫切於謹獨也。能致慎而不忽焉，尚何離道之遠哉？中庸論率性之道，以明由教而入。至此，蓋謂道具于心，固當養於未動之時，尤當省於方動之始。何則？幽暗之中，踪跡邃密，人莫能窺其際，可謂隱也。然念慮初萌，而邪正攸判，人雖不覩也，已則了然於胸中，見之之真，莫可得而掩矣。舉天下之著見者，孰有過於隱乎？細微之事，端緒眇忽，人莫能測其機，可謂微也。然思惟甫動，而善惡遂分，人雖未聞也，已則昭然於方寸，知之之切，莫可得而揜矣。極天下之明顯者，孰有踰於微乎？夫幾微之動，明著如此，苟或肆焉，則人欲滋長於獨知之際，而馴至離道之遠矣。是以君子既嘗戒懼矣，而於此尤加謹焉。因其所發之初，隨致省察之力，一念之邪，即遏絕之，務使邪不得以撓正，而惕乎儆戒之弗寧，不以人所不知而侈然以自放也。因其方萌之始，隨加點檢之功，一念之惡，即禁制之，務期惡不得以混善，而凛
translation_en:
…the incipient movements of the heart are nowhere more manifest than in what is hidden and subtle, and nothing is more essential to self-examination than vigilance when alone. If one exercises the utmost care without neglect, how could one stray far from the Way? The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the Way of following one’s nature to clarify how one enters it through instruction. At this point, its meaning is that the Way is inherent in the heart: one must certainly nurture it before any movement arises, but must especially examine it at the very beginning of movement. Why is this? Amid darkness, traces lie deeply concealed, and no one can glimpse their bounds: this may be called hidden. Yet as thoughts first sprout, the deviant and the upright are distinguished. Though others do not see them, they are already clear within one’s own breast; the clarity with which one sees them cannot be concealed. Of all that is manifest under Heaven, what surpasses the hidden? In minute affairs, the first indications are faint and fleeting, and no one can fathom their incipient workings: this may be called subtle. Yet as thinking first stirs, good and evil immediately separate. Though others have not heard of them, they are already manifest within one’s own heart; the immediacy with which one knows them cannot be concealed. Of all that is evident under Heaven, what exceeds the subtle?

Since these incipient, subtle movements are so plainly manifest, if one gives them free rein, human desires will grow at the point known to oneself alone, gradually leading one far from the Way. Thus, although the gentleman already exercises caution and apprehension, he is especially vigilant here. At the very outset of a thought’s emergence, he immediately applies the effort of self-examination. A single deviant thought he at once checks and cuts off, striving to prevent deviation from disturbing rectitude. Alert and unremitting in his vigilance, he does not indulge himself without restraint merely because others do not know. At the very beginning of a thought’s sprouting, he immediately applies the work of scrutiny. A single evil thought he at once restrains, striving to prevent evil from mingling with good, and, in awe…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
乎警省之無已不以人所不覺而偃然以自恣
也如是則私欲窒而人心之危者以安本體全
而道心之微者以著體道者可不知所務哉嗚
呼莫難審者其惟幾乎故大舜之惟精顏子有
不善未嘗不知皆是道也子思憂道學失傳於
此不得不詳言體道之方以詔後世而世又有
所見涉於疑似彌近理而大亂眞者則去道又
遠矣是以君子又在乎窮理也理明則見自正
而守自篤大學言格物先於正心良有以哉
===
君正莫不正一正君而國定矣
林維藩
考試官訓導王批揭書出題本無深
意作者多於一正君處深求重講
殊失朱註此篇轉換數語而其義
了然是用錄之
考試官教諭劉批發新奇於平易中
而有矩度佳作也
大賢推人君心正之善而及國治之由以見人
punctuated:
乎警省之無已，不以人所不覺而偃然以自恣也。如是，則私欲窒而人心之危者以安，本體全而道心之微者以著。體道者可不知所務哉？嗚呼！莫難審者，其惟幾乎！故大舜之惟精，顏子有不善未嘗不知，皆是道也。子思憂道學失傳，於此不得不詳言體道之方，以詔後世。而世又有所見涉於疑似，彌近理而大亂眞者，則去道又遠矣。是以君子又在乎窮理也。理明則見自正，而守自篤。《大學》言格物先於正心，良有以哉！

君正，莫不正；一正君而國定矣。
林維藩

考試官訓導王批：「揭書出題，本無深意。作者多於一正君處深求重講，殊失朱註。此篇轉換數語，而其義了然，是用錄之。」

考試官教諭劉批：「發新奇於平易中，而有矩度，佳作也。」

大賢推人君心正之善，而及國治之由，以見人
translation_en:
…unceasingly vigilant and introspective, he does not complacently indulge himself merely because others are unaware. In this way, selfish desires are checked and the precarious human mind is brought to peace; the original substance is preserved whole and the subtle moral mind becomes manifest. Can one who embodies the Way fail to understand what to attend to? Alas! Is anything harder to discern than the first stirrings of thought? Thus, the great Shun’s injunction to be discerning, and Master Yan’s never failing to recognize any fault in himself, both express this Way. Zisi, concerned that the learning of the Way might cease to be transmitted, could not but explain here in detail how to embody the Way, thereby instructing later generations. Yet there are also those whose views stray into specious ambiguities: the closer these seem to principle, the more profoundly they confound truth, taking them still farther from the Way. Thus the gentleman must also devote himself to investigating principle fully. When principle is clear, his understanding will naturally be correct and his adherence naturally firm. There is good reason indeed that the Great Learning places the investigation of things before the rectification of the mind!

“When the ruler is upright, none will fail to be upright; once the ruler is rectified, the state will be settled.”
Lin Weifan

Comment by Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “The passage selected from the book as the examination topic originally has no hidden meaning. Most writers probe too deeply into ‘once the ruler is rectified’ and give it excessive exposition, seriously missing the sense of Zhu Xi’s commentary. This essay varies the phrasing in a few places and makes the meaning perfectly clear. For this reason it has been included.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “It brings forth something fresh and striking from what is plain and straightforward, while remaining within proper bounds. An excellent composition.”

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
臣當以正君爲急也蓋君心之善國治之功一
皆大人正君之所致也然則爲人臣者可不急
先務哉昔孟子之意以爲大人之事君也不以
用人行政爲急而獨以正君爲急者何哉蓋以
人君之心攻之者衆私意一萌見於用者皆邪
矣夫旣格之而歸於仁焉則所存者正而有以
立天下之□□非心一動發於事者多枉矣夫
旣格之而□於義焉則所主者正而有以凝天
下之大道□□正朝廷以正□□舉直錯枉咸
===
得其宜無□□授自無偏□□□之私也何往
而不正耶□□官以正萬民□□陳紀各當其
可庶政之□□爲公平正大之體也何適而非
正耶夫君心□□□□□此所以大人之事君
不瑣瑣於人之間也唯以正君而爲要焉一正
其君則百爲之度以貞矣措之於國尚何有不
治乎不屑屑於政之間也唯以正君而爲急焉
君心一正則萬化之源以清矣施之於國抑何
有不定乎將見一人元良而百辟刑之君子盡
punctuated: 臣當以正君爲急也。蓋君心之善、國治之功，一皆大人正君之所致也。然則爲人臣者，可不急先務哉？昔孟子之意，以爲大人之事君也，不以用人行政爲急，而獨以正君爲急者，何哉？蓋以人君之心，攻之者衆，私意一萌，見於用者皆邪矣。夫旣格之而歸於仁焉，則所存者正，而有以立天下之□□。非心一動，發於事者多枉矣。夫旣格之而□於義焉，則所主者正，而有以凝天下之大道。□□正朝廷以正□□，舉直錯枉，咸得其宜，無□□授，自無偏□□□之私也。何往而不正耶？□□官以正萬民，□□陳紀，各當其可，庶政之□□爲公平正大之體也。何適而非正耶？夫君心□□□□□，此所以大人之事君，不瑣瑣於人之間也，唯以正君而爲要焉。一正其君，則百爲之度以貞矣，措之於國，尚何有不治乎？不屑屑於政之間也，唯以正君而爲急焉。君心一正，則萬化之源以清矣，施之於國，抑何有不定乎？將見一人元良而百辟刑之，君子盡
translation_en:
…a minister should make rectifying his ruler his urgent concern. For the goodness of the ruler’s heart and the achievement of order in the state are all brought about by the great man’s rectification of the ruler. Can one who serves as a minister, then, fail to give urgency to what must come first? What Mencius meant was this: why does the great man, in serving his ruler, regard neither the employment of men nor the conduct of government as his urgent concern, but regard only rectifying the ruler as urgent? It is because many things assail the ruler’s heart. Once a selfish intention sprouts, everything manifested in his actions becomes deviant. Once the great man has corrected him and brought him back to benevolence, however, what he holds in his heart is upright, and thereby he can establish the realm’s [two illegible characters]. Once a wrongful thought stirs, much that issues forth in affairs becomes crooked. Once the great man has corrected him and [illegible character] him to righteousness [?], however, what he takes as his guiding principle is upright, and thereby he can consolidate the Great Way of the realm.

[Text missing] rectifies the court in order to rectify [text missing]; raising up the upright and setting aside the crooked are both done fittingly. There is no [text missing] bestowal [?], and naturally there is no selfish partiality [text missing]. Wherever he turns, how could anything fail to be upright? [Text missing] officials, in order to rectify all the people; [text missing] setting forth the governing rules, each as is fitting. The [text missing] of the many affairs of government constitute a system that is fair, impartial, upright, and open. Wherever he turns, how could anything be other than upright?

Now, the ruler’s heart [five illegible characters]. This is why the great man, in serving his ruler, does not busy himself with petty details concerning personnel, but takes rectifying his ruler as the essential task. Once he has rectified his ruler, the standards for all undertakings become correct. When this is put into effect in the state, how could it still fail to be well governed? He does not fuss over the details of administration, but takes rectifying his ruler as his urgent concern. Once the ruler’s heart is upright, the source of all transforming influences becomes pure. When this is applied to the state, how could it fail to become settled? Then we shall see the One Man supremely virtuous, with all the officials taking him as their model, and all the gentlemen…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
得以爲國謀也群小不得以摇國是也治隆於
上俗美於下宗社由之而奠安矣夫何顛覆之
足患哉一人有慶而兆民賴之良法自足以壽
國脉也匪彞不得以亂國與也遠之有望近之
不厭邦家由之而底綏矣夫何危亡之足憂哉
是則國不自定也本于君心之正心不易正也
資於大人之德爲人臣者可不知所務耶抑觀
伊尹樂堯舜之道故能格太甲之非而有處仁
遷義之美周公備元聖之德故能格成王之非
===
而成刑措不用之治大人之功不其偉耶獨慨
夫魯哀齊宣親遇孔孟不聞有所感悟徒起夫
美矣至矣之嘆委諸好勇好貨好色之疾使齊
魯之國終無一變之幾良可惜哉吁聖賢之所
能者人也所不能者天也吾於孔孟乎何憾
易
利用爲大作元吉无咎
趙鼒
同考試官訓導高批居下受益貴於盡
punctuated:
得以爲國謀也，群小不得以摇國是也。治隆於上，俗美於下，宗社由之而奠安矣，夫何顛覆之足患哉！一人有慶而兆民賴之，良法自足以壽國脉也，匪彞不得以亂國與也。遠之有望，近之不厭，邦家由之而底綏矣，夫何危亡之足憂哉！是則國不自定也，本于君心之正；心不易正也，資於大人之德。爲人臣者，可不知所務耶？抑觀伊尹樂堯舜之道，故能格太甲之非，而有處仁遷義之美；周公備元聖之德，故能格成王之非，而成刑措不用之治。大人之功，不其偉耶？獨慨夫魯哀、齊宣親遇孔孟，不聞有所感悟，徒起夫「美矣！至矣！」之嘆，委諸好勇、好貨、好色之疾，使齊魯之國終無一變之幾，良可惜哉！吁！聖賢之所能者，人也；所不能者，天也。吾於孔孟乎何憾？

易
利用爲大作，元吉，无咎。
趙鼒

同考試官訓導高批：居下受益，貴於盡
translation_en:
…are able to deliberate on behalf of the state, while petty men cannot unsettle its settled policies. Good government flourishes above, and customs improve below; the ancestral temples and altars of state are thereby secured. What cause, then, is there to fear overthrow? When the one ruler enjoys blessings, the myriad people benefit from them. Sound laws themselves suffice to prolong the life of the state, and departures from established norms cannot throw the state into disorder [?]. Those far away look toward him with hope, and those nearby never tire of him. The realm thereby attains peace. What cause, then, is there to fear peril and ruin?

Thus, the state does not become stable of itself: its stability rests on the rectitude of the ruler’s heart. Nor is the heart easily rectified: this requires the virtue of a great man. Can those who serve as ministers fail to understand what they must attend to? Consider Yi Yin: he delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun, and thus could correct Tai Jia’s faults, bringing about the admirable result that Tai Jia dwelt in benevolence and moved toward righteousness. The Duke of Zhou possessed the virtue of a supreme sage, and thus could correct King Cheng’s faults and achieve a government in which punishments were set aside and left unused. Are not the achievements of great men magnificent?

Yet one can only lament that Duke Ai of Lu and King Xuan of Qi personally encountered Confucius and Mencius, but are not known to have been moved to understanding. They merely exclaimed, “How fine! How perfect!” and gave themselves over to their weaknesses for valor, wealth, and sensual pleasure. Consequently, the states of Qi and Lu never had even the beginnings of a transformation. How truly regrettable! Alas! What sages and worthies can accomplish belongs to the human sphere; what they cannot accomplish belongs to Heaven. What cause have I to find fault with Confucius and Mencius?

Book of Changes
“It is beneficial to undertake great works. Supreme good fortune; no blame.”
Zhao Zi

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
善而子能發之他日見用慎勿忘
斯言也
考試官訓導王批寫出臣子報益之
心可愛取之不但文耳
考試官教諭劉批文從理順似亦大
作
宜圖大以報益必盡善以免愆蓋人臣受知固
以圖大爲宜而尤以盡善爲美也不然曷足以
免其愆哉聖人繫益爻如此其意以爲益之初
===
九以陽居下受上之益當斯時也情誼結於下
交之初膏澤覃於大賚之始臣子之心豈可徒
然無所報哉要必舉脩於家者悉達於有道之
朝以學於幼者咸行於可爲之日不規規於細
務也而凡告之於君措之於民者皆經綸天下
之宏規庶於平世而相宜矣不屑屑於末事也
而凡議之於廷達之於政者皆開闔造化之偉
績斯於昌期而不負矣然處卑而任大多涉非
分之嫌居下而得君每招援上之議必其凡所
punctuated:
善，而子能發之。他日見用，慎勿忘斯言也。

考試官訓導王批：寫出臣子報益之心，可愛。取之，不但文耳。

考試官教諭劉批：文從理順，似亦大作。

宜圖大以報益，必盡善以免愆。蓋人臣受知，固以圖大爲宜，而尤以盡善爲美也。不然，曷足以免其愆哉？聖人繫益爻如此，其意以爲益之初九，以陽居下，受上之益。當斯時也，情誼結於下交之初，膏澤覃於大賚之始，臣子之心豈可徒然無所報哉？要必舉脩於家者，悉達於有道之朝；以學於幼者，咸行於可爲之日。不規規於細務也，而凡告之於君、措之於民者，皆經綸天下之宏規，庶於平世而相宜矣。不屑屑於末事也，而凡議之於廷、達之於政者，皆開闔造化之偉績，斯於昌期而不負矣。然處卑而任大，多涉非分之嫌；居下而得君，每招援上之議。必其凡所
translation_en:
…goodness, and you have succeeded in bringing this out. When you are employed in office hereafter, take care never to forget these words.

Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It expresses the heart of a subject intent on repaying benefits received: admirable. I select it for more than its literary merit alone.”

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The writing flows and the reasoning is coherent; this too seems a great undertaking.”

One should plan great undertakings to repay benefits received, and must achieve complete goodness to avoid fault. When a minister receives his ruler’s recognition, it is certainly fitting that he plan great undertakings; yet complete goodness is especially to be prized. Otherwise, how could he avoid fault? Such is the meaning of the words the sage appended to this line of the hexagram Increase. The initial nine of Increase, a yang line occupying the lowest position, receives benefits from above. At such a time, affection and loyalty are bound together as the ruler first enters into relations with those below, and beneficence spreads as great gifts begin to be bestowed. How could a subject’s heart remain unmoved, making no repayment? He must bring everything cultivated at home fully into service at a court possessing the Way, and put everything learned in youth into practice at a time when action is possible. He must not confine himself narrowly to petty tasks: everything he proposes to his ruler or implements among the people must form part of a grand plan for ordering the realm, so that it may accord with an age of peace. He must not busy himself with trifling matters: everything he discusses at court or carries into government must contribute to magnificent achievements that guide the workings of creation. Thus he will not fail an age of flourishing rule. Yet occupying a humble position while assuming great responsibilities often arouses suspicion of overstepping one’s proper station; holding low rank while enjoying the ruler’s favor regularly invites accusations of reaching upward for support. title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
行者至公無私以協天下之公論可以施之於
近而無訾也行之於遠而無弊也務期盡善而
不爲目前之計可焉凡所爲者至誠無偽以合
聖賢之成法可以參諸人情而不悖也揆諸事
體而無乖也務底至善而不爲隨世之圖可焉
如是則在已免冒濫之耻在人無指摘之尤雖
曰受上之益而反躬自無愧也智小謀大之咎
何有哉雖曰膺君之寵而拊心自無怍也力小
任重之誚奚有哉是則欲報稱者乃臣子之心
===
欲至善者乃盡瘁之義居下而受上之益者固
如是哉嗚呼天下之事不難於行已之志而難
於得君之心苟扞格焉雖以周公之大勳勞亦
不免成王之疑也况於下者乎况於小臣乎是
故又在乎守之以敬而持之以謙耳惟敬足以
感君惟謙足以處衆而事業之成無難也不然
雖盡善乎大作寧免意外之咎哉故孔子謂事
上也敬又曰謙也者致恭以存其位也噫聖人
斯言其亦洞照萬世之人心與
punctuated:
行者至公無私，以協天下之公論，可以施之於近而無訾也，行之於遠而無弊也，務期盡善而不爲目前之計可焉。凡所爲者至誠無偽，以合聖賢之成法，可以參諸人情而不悖也，揆諸事體而無乖也，務底至善而不爲隨世之圖可焉。如是，則在已免冒濫之耻，在人無指摘之尤。雖曰受上之益，而反躬自無愧也，智小謀大之咎何有哉？雖曰膺君之寵，而拊心自無怍也，力小任重之誚奚有哉？是則欲報稱者，乃臣子之心；欲至善者，乃盡瘁之義。居下而受上之益者，固如是哉！

嗚呼！天下之事，不難於行已之志，而難於得君之心。苟扞格焉，雖以周公之大勳勞，亦不免成王之疑也，况於下者乎？况於小臣乎？是故又在乎守之以敬，而持之以謙耳。惟敬足以感君，惟謙足以處衆，而事業之成無難也。不然，雖盡善乎大作，寧免意外之咎哉？故孔子謂：「事上也敬。」又曰：「謙也者，致恭以存其位也。」噫！聖人斯言，其亦洞照萬世之人心與？
translation_en:
…all his actions must be utterly impartial and free of selfishness, in accord with the public judgment of all under Heaven. They can then be put into practice nearby without reproach and carried out afar without harmful consequences. He must strive for complete goodness, making no calculations merely for immediate advantage. Everything he does must be utterly sincere and without deception, conforming to the established models of the sages and worthies. It can then be tested against human feelings without contradiction and measured against the circumstances of affairs without discrepancy. He must strive to attain the highest goodness, making no plans merely to conform to prevailing ways. Thus he will personally escape the shame of claiming what he does not deserve, and give others no grounds for criticism. Though he receives benefits from above, he will feel no shame upon examining himself: how could he incur the blame of having little wisdom yet devising great plans? Though he enjoys his ruler’s favor, he will feel no shame when searching his heart: how could he incur the reproach of having little strength yet bearing a heavy responsibility? The desire to make a fitting return is the heart of a loyal subject; the desire to attain the highest goodness expresses the duty of serving to the utmost. Surely this is how one who occupies a subordinate position and receives benefits from above should act!

Alas! In the affairs of the world, the difficulty lies less in carrying out one’s own intentions than in winning the ruler’s heart. If there is discord, even the Duke of Zhou, with his great meritorious service, could not escape King Cheng’s suspicion. How much more so for those of lower standing! How much more so for a minor official! Thus one must also uphold these principles with reverence and sustain them with humility. Reverence alone suffices to move the ruler; humility alone suffices to live harmoniously among others. Then bringing one’s undertakings to completion will present no difficulty. Otherwise, even if one achieves complete goodness in great undertakings, how can one escape unforeseen blame? Thus Confucius said, “In serving his superiors, he was reverent.” He also said, “Humility means showing the utmost respect so as to preserve one’s position.” Ah! Do not these words of the sage penetrate and illuminate the hearts of people through all ages?

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
爻也者效此者也象也者像此者也
楊翼
同考試官訓導高批說者泥於章首四
爻謂此爻字即指六爻言不必從
始初一畫說來然則章首象字乃
指一卦言亦可遺六十四卦乎蓋
大傳本互文以見意觀因重字則
次序可知此卷□也知此其說效
像處意更親切非素潜心於易者
===
未足語此
考試官訓導王批見□明而措詞雅
作易義當如是矣
考試官教諭劉批乾坤易簡即天理
流行發見之實聖人仰觀俯察為
爻象以法之人人皆知也而未見
有發揮至此者
大傳原夫易書之作惟法乎易簡之理而已蓋
天地有自然之易卦爻不過效而象之爾夫豈
punctuated:
「爻也者，效此者也；象也者，像此者也。」
楊翼

同考試官訓導高批：說者泥於章首四爻，謂此爻字即指六爻言，不必從始初一畫說來。然則章首象字乃指一卦言，亦可遺六十四卦乎？蓋大傳本互文以見意，觀因重字，則次序可知。此卷□也知此，其說效像處，意更親切。非素潜心於易者，未足語此。

考試官訓導王批：見□明而措詞雅，作易義當如是矣。

考試官教諭劉批：乾坤易簡，即天理流行發見之實。聖人仰觀俯察，為爻象以法之，人人皆知也，而未見有發揮至此者。

大傳原夫易書之作，惟法乎易簡之理而已。蓋天地有自然之易，卦爻不過效而象之爾。夫豈
translation_en:
“The lines imitate this; the images represent this.”
Yang Yi 楊翼

Comment by Associate Examiner Gao, Assistant Instructor: Interpreters cling to the “four lines” [?] at the beginning of the chapter, claiming that the word “lines” here refers specifically to the six lines, and that there is no need to begin the explanation with the very first stroke. But then, if the word “images” at the beginning of the chapter refers to a single hexagram, may one likewise omit the sixty-four hexagrams? The Great Commentary uses mutually complementary wording to convey its meaning. From the words “following upon” and “doubling,” the sequence can be understood. This essay [illegible] also understands this; its explanation of “imitating” and “representing” is all the more apt in meaning. Someone who had not long devoted himself to studying the Changes could not discuss this.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: The understanding [illegible] is clear, and the phrasing elegant. An essay on the meaning of the Changes should indeed be like this.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The ease and simplicity of Qian and Kun are precisely the actual operation and manifestation of Heaven’s principle. The sages observed above and examined below, making lines and images to model it. Everyone knows this, yet I have never seen anyone elucidate it to this extent.

The Great Commentary traces the origins of the making of the Book of Changes: it did no more than model the principle of ease and simplicity. For Heaven and Earth possess their own spontaneous Changes; the hexagrams and lines merely imitate and represent them. How could it possibly …

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
作意於其間哉大傳此章言卦爻吉凶及此謂
夫造化无言也常以易簡而示人聖人有見也
必假爻象以顯義夫易之初作惟有爻爾而形
分竒偶自夫始為一畫以分陰陽次為二畫以
分太少倍之而為三重之而為六而竒偶錯綜
之不一豈假於安排乎不過效夫乾坤之易簡
而已是故竒之形即模擬至健之天道偶之畫
即彷彿至順之地德周流乎六虚者固皆太極
動静之運行變動於二體者亦皆一元通復之
===
貫徹蓋无朕之中而无窮之數已具特假易爻
發之爾若乃爻之既畫斯成象矣而時有消息
觀夫始於二純六爻成於一貞八悔或為陽長
陰消之卦或為陰長陽消之卦而消息相因之
无窮夫豈出於臆見乎不過象夫乾坤之易簡
而已是故陽長陰消則黙寓乎確然之性情陰
長陽消則顯設夫隤然之法象變易以從道莫
非易知簡能之至理交易以隨時孰非知始作
成之妙用蓋无極之前而有象之器已含但假
punctuated: 作意於其間哉？大傳此章言卦爻吉凶，及此謂夫造化无言也，常以易簡而示人；聖人有見也，必假爻象以顯義。夫易之初作，惟有爻爾，而形分竒偶。自夫始為一畫以分陰陽，次為二畫以分太少，倍之而為三，重之而為六，而竒偶錯綜之不一，豈假於安排乎？不過效夫乾坤之易簡而已。是故竒之形，即模擬至健之天道；偶之畫，即彷彿至順之地德。周流乎六虚者，固皆太極動静之運行；變動於二體者，亦皆一元通復之貫徹。蓋无朕之中，而无窮之數已具，特假易爻發之爾。若乃爻之既畫，斯成象矣，而時有消息。觀夫始於二純六爻，成於一貞八悔，或為陽長陰消之卦，或為陰長陽消之卦，而消息相因之无窮，夫豈出於臆見乎？不過象夫乾坤之易簡而已。是故陽長陰消，則黙寓乎確然之性情；陰長陽消，則顯設夫隤然之法象。變易以從道，莫非易知簡能之至理；交易以隨時，孰非知始作成之妙用？蓋无極之前，而有象之器已含，但假
translation_en:
…deliberately contrive anything within it? This chapter of the Great Commentary discusses the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of hexagrams and lines, and at this point means that the transforming processes of creation speak no words, yet constantly reveal themselves to people through ease and simplicity. The sages possess insight and must draw upon the lines and images to make their meaning manifest.

When the Changes was first made, there were only lines, whose forms were divided into odd and even. Beginning with a single line to distinguish yin and yang, then proceeding to two lines to distinguish the greater and lesser forms, the combinations were doubled to make three lines and stacked to make six. With odd and even interwoven in their many configurations, could this have depended upon deliberate arrangement? It merely emulated the ease and simplicity of Qian and Kun. Thus, the odd line’s form models the Way of Heaven in its utmost vigor, while the even line’s strokes resemble the virtue of Earth in its utmost compliance. What circulates through the six empty positions is entirely the movement and stillness of the Supreme Ultimate in operation; what changes within the two constituent trigrams is likewise the single primal force pervading them through its passage and return. Within that which shows no trace, inexhaustible numerical patterns are already complete: the lines of the Changes merely serve to disclose them.

Once the lines have been drawn, images are formed, and waxing and waning occur with the times. Consider how these begin with the six lines of the two pure hexagrams and reach completion through one inner trigram and eight outer trigrams. Some hexagrams show yang increasing and yin diminishing; others show yin increasing and yang diminishing. This waxing and waning follows in an endless succession. Could it arise from subjective conjecture? It merely represents the ease and simplicity of Qian and Kun. Thus, when yang increases and yin diminishes, the firm and steadfast nature and disposition are silently embodied; when yin increases and yang diminishes, the yielding patterns and images are visibly displayed. In changing to follow the Way, all embody the ultimate principle of knowing through ease and accomplishing through simplicity. In interchanging to accord with the times, all manifest the wondrous efficacy of directing beginnings and bringing things to completion. Even before the Limitless, concrete things possessing images were already contained within it; it merely draws upon…

title: 嘉靖四年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
卦畫泄之爾是則聖人畫卦作易之本旨皆原
於天地自然之理如此易書冒天下之道也不
以是哉大抵天地畫前之易也唯聖人為能契
之使夫人皆聖人也則何所事夫易哉故曰天
何言哉予欲無言易之作聖人為天下後世而
設也稽實待虛則在乎學易者心玩而身體焉
然後信其為大哉易也夫體易亦非易易事也
故又曰神而明之存乎其人
書
===
敷納以言明庶以功
□維藩
考試官訓導王批虞廷敷對雍容氣
象自難摹寫此作於悠揚暢達之
中有雅勁嚴肅之趣足覘所養之
不凡矣
考試官教諭劉批即理致之言其平
日體認之功於是乎驗
大臣期君之用賢旣當觀其所蘊又當考其所
banxin: 山東鄉試錄 三十六
punctuated:
卦畫泄之爾。是則聖人畫卦作易之本旨，皆原於天地自然之理如此。《易》書冒天下之道也，不以是哉？大抵天地，畫前之易也，唯聖人為能契之。使夫人皆聖人也，則何所事夫《易》哉？故曰：「天何言哉？予欲無言。」《易》之作，聖人為天下後世而設也。稽實待虛，則在乎學《易》者心玩而身體焉，然後信其為大哉《易》也。夫體《易》亦非易易事也，故又曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」
書
敷納以言，明庶以功。
□維藩
考試官訓導王批：「虞廷敷對，雍容氣象，自難摹寫。此作於悠揚暢達之中，有雅勁嚴肅之趣，足覘所養之不凡矣。」
考試官教諭劉批：「即理致之言，其平日體認之功，於是乎驗。」
大臣期君之用賢，旣當觀其所蘊，又當考其所
translation_en:
…the drawn hexagrams merely disclose it. Thus the sages’ fundamental purpose in drawing the hexagrams and composing the Book of Changes was entirely grounded in the natural principles of Heaven and Earth. Is this not why the Book of Changes encompasses the Way of all under Heaven? Broadly speaking, Heaven and Earth are the Changes before the hexagrams were drawn; only the sages could accord with them. If everyone were a sage, what need would there be for the Book of Changes? Hence the sayings: “What does Heaven say?” and “I wish to say nothing.” The sages composed the Book of Changes for all under Heaven and for later generations. To examine what is actual and await what has yet to become manifest depends upon students of the Changes pondering it in their hearts and embodying it in their conduct. Only then will they truly believe how great the Changes is. Yet embodying the Changes is no easy matter. Hence it is also said: “To comprehend it spiritually and illuminate it rests with the person.”
Book of Documents
“Receive them broadly on the basis of their words; distinguish them all by their accomplishments.”
□ Weifan
Comment by Examiner Wang, Assistant Instructor: “The poised and dignified atmosphere of replies delivered at the court of Shun is inherently difficult to portray. Amid its flowing ease and fluency, this composition has an elegant strength and solemn gravity, sufficient to reveal the exceptional quality of the writer’s cultivation.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: “These words accord with the import of principle; they attest to his habitual efforts to grasp it through personal experience.”
